5. Historical Data Collection

The observed data report on the pH of the upper 5 meters of the ocean. Each data set covers a different time period:

  • BATS data used in this indicator are available from 1983 to 2015. Samples were collected from two locations in the Atlantic Ocean near Bermuda (BATS and Hydrostation S, at 31°43' N, 64°10' W; and 32°10’ N, 64°30’ W, respectively).
  • ESTOC data are available from 1995 to 2009. ESTOC is at 29°10’ N, 15°30’ W in the Atlantic Ocean.
  • CARIACO data are available from 1995 to 2017. The CARIACO station is at 10.5° N, 64.67° W in the Caribbean Sea: specifically, the Cariaco Basin off the coast of Venezuela.
  • HOT data are available from 1988 to 2022. The HOT station is at 23° N, 158° W in the Pacific Ocean.

At ESTOC and CARIACO, pH and alkalinity were measured directly. For BATS and HOT, pH was derived from other measured parameters as described in the technical documentation for EPA’s Ocean Acidity indicator. That technical documentation also provides links and publications that lay out each station’s internally consistent sampling protocols. All four stations have reported values at approximately monthly intervals, though exact timing varies by station, and there are some small gaps.

6. Indicator Derivation

Observed Data

For all four locations, the graphs show in situ measured or calculated values for pH, as opposed to values adjusted to a standard temperature. The project team also did not attempt to adjust for seasonal variability. The time between reported sampling events is somewhat irregular at all four locations, so moving averages and monthly or annual averages based on these data could be misleading. Thus, the project team elected to show individual measurements, which have approximately monthly resolution, and which offer the benefit of showing the sometimes-sizable seasonal variations inherent in ocean acidity.

Model Outputs

The project team identified the GCM output grid cells in which each of the stations are located. The Bermuda site had two stations in different cells, so the team averaged the results from those two cells. The team performed the following steps via R and Python scripts:

  • The team aggregated the seven models using the standard Bayesian model weighting approach used in the Fifth National Climate Assessment and documented by Massoud et al. (2023). Because the standard weighting is based on 16 models, the authors of Massoud et al. (2023) provided corresponding weights for the subset of seven models used here.
  • The team averaged the GCM monthly grids to generate annual means, then further smoothed the weighted average modeled results using an 11-year moving average. The team performed this step independently for the hindcast (through 2014) and for each scenario from 2015 (the first year of divergence) forward.
  • The team retained monthly GCM resolution in calculating 10th to 90th percentile ranges for the graphs.

7. Alignment

Observations were generally centered within the range of modeled values for all sites. Thus, no bias correction or other transformation was necessary.

8. Display

The interactive graphs for this pairing show the following elements:

  • Observed data from EPA’s indicator from 1983 to 2022. Some sites only have data for portions of this range. Sub-annual resolution from EPA’s indicator has been retained to show how pH varies throughout the year.
  • Modeled hindcast from 1950 to 2014. The line on each graph shows the Bayesian weighted average of the seven GCMs, smoothed using an 11-year moving average. The resulting 11-year means are plotted from 1955 to 2009, as the project team did not attempt to apply any endpoint padding at either end of the series.
  • Modeled projections from 2015 to 2100 for four emissions scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5), with 2014 added for continuity (2014 is the last year before the scenarios diverge). Each scenario line on the graph shows the Bayesian weighted average of the seven GCMs, smoothed using an 11-year moving average. The resulting 11-year means are plotted starting at 2014 to provide continuity with the hindcast annual ranges, although the scenarios do not start to diverge until 2015. Smoothed values for 2014–2019 pick up some hindcast years in the average. The 11-year means are plotted through 2095, including data from 2090 through 2100, the last year of available data. Scenarios have been assigned “plain-language” names for consistency throughout this pairings effort.
  • A shaded band around each of the scenarios, reflecting the 10th to 90th percentiles among the seven models. This shaded band therefore illustrates the range of modeled values. The shaded bands show original monthly values to provide a sense of how the intra-annual variations shown in the observed data set will continue into the future; they have not been smoothed. The projected ranges start in 2014 to provide continuity with the hindcast, but the scenarios begin to diverge in 2015.

9. Quality Assurance and Quality Control

The technical documentation for the Ocean Acidity indicator provides references that address the quality assurance and quality control steps followed during observed data collection and data analysis. Quality procedures for each GCM (e.g., validation) are described in source papers published by the organizations that have developed and run each model; these sources are available through links in the overall technical documentation [to be linked] for this effort. For each pairing, the project team conducted typical quality control steps, including independently checking all aggregations, unit conversions, transformations, and other calculations.
